Indonesia has suspended flights at its main international airport outside Jakarta, after volcanic ash from the erupting Mount Anak Krakatau spread over the capital. Soekarno-Hatta international airport, more than 150km (93 miles) from the volcano, said on Sunday it had halted operations until 5:30pm local time (10:30 GMT), stranding hundreds of passengers. The suspension has affected 301 flights, including 58 international services, airport operator Angkasa Pura said in a statement on Sunday. Singapore Airlines said it had cancelled flights to and from Jakarta for the rest of the day.
